subject: Re: TheraQuell — multi-year pricing / renewal protection request
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@theraquell.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-08T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Multi-year ask after pilot — price lock + renewal protection

Hi Tessa,

Really enjoyed the pilot wrap-up yesterday. Our exec team is aligned on moving to a three-year commitment if we can get two commercial protections in place: a firm price lock for the first 24 months and a renewal-protection clause that caps any post-term uplift to a percentage (we suggested 7%) or CPI — whichever is lower.

Key context:
- We expect predictable spend for product roadmap planning and want to avoid surprise increases during our rollout.
- We are open to a blended commit and willing to sign an upfront invoice schedule for year 1 to help with Redwood's cash visibility.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can offer: 1) a 24-month price lock, 2) an uplift cap on renewals, and 3) an option to add annual reserved capacity increases at fixed unit pricing?

Attaching the baseline SOW and our procurement timeline. We need final commercial terms and an executed SOW by end of month to hit our board milestones.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Platform Partnerships
TheraQuell Health
[Attachment: TheraQuell_SOW_inbound.pdf (pdf, 2 pages)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@theraquell.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@theraquell.com>
Date: 2027-09-08T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Multi-year ask after pilot — price lock + renewal protection

Ben/Laura — forwarding TheraQuell's commercial asks. Short summary and ask below.

Summary: customer willing to commit to 3 years; requires:
- 24-month hard price lock (no per-token/unit increases for first 24 months)
- Renewal protection: uplift cap of <=7% on renewal or CPI whichever lower
- Option to scale reserved capacity at fixed per-unit price for additional committed GPU months
- Upfront payment for year 1 accepted (helps Redwood cash flow)

Financial impact (see attached Deal_Econ):
- List price ARR (year 1 blended): $1.8M
- Customer requests blended discount such that effective ARR year1 ~ $1.35M (approx 25% blended) — this yields a gross margin hit vs plan of ~9 points in year1 but is back-loaded over term by committed revenue.

My ask: Exec approval to sign these commercial protections with the following constraints:
1) Limit blended discount to <= 25% for year1 and <= 12% year2 (net of committed reserved capacity).
2) Price lock to apply to the actual SKU pricing Redwood invoices (no guarantees on future new SKUs).
3) Renewal uplift cap to be 7% and tied to CPI floor/ceiling language handled by Legal.
4) Add mutual churn protection: customer can request termination with 60 days notice for material breaches; Redwood retains right to transition to standard pricing if they exceed committed capacity by >20%.

Please review the Deal_Econ_TheraQuell.xlsx and the SOW redlines I drafted (SOW_redlines_3yr.docx). If you can sign off, I'll prepare the Exec Approval Memo and route to Finance for the DocuSign envelope. We need a yes/no today to keep their timeline.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Deal_Econ_TheraQuell.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-08T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Multi-year ask after pilot — price lock + renewal protection

Tessa — quick thoughts inline.

On 9/8/27 11:02 AM, Tessa Morgan wrote:
> Financial impact (see attached Deal_Econ):
> - List price ARR (year 1 blended): $1.8M
> - Customer requests blended discount such that effective ARR year1 ~ $1.35M (approx 25% blended) — this yields a gross margin hit vs plan of ~9 points in year1 but is back-loaded over term by committed revenue.

We can tolerate a one-off margin compression if the ARR is solid and contractually committed. Need to confirm: are they buying Dedicated capacity or Hosted API consumption? If Dedicated, the economics are better.

On the uplift cap + price lock: I want to push for a 2-year lock (they asked 24 months — ok) but limit the lock to current published SKUs and exclude newly introduced premium SKUs. Also recommend an annual true-up clause for over-usage.

Approval ask for Exec: if terms match below, I can greenlight from Deal Desk and escalate for Finance sign-off:
- Blended discount cap: 25% year1 / 12% year2 max
- Price lock: 24 months on current SKUs only
- Renewal uplift cap: 7% + CPI language (no other hidden fees)
- Prepayment for year1 preferred (30 days net invoicing)

If Laura is good, we can draft Exec_Approval_Memo and route to CFO.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@theraquell.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@theraquell.com>
Date: 2027-09-09T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Multi-year ask after pilot — price lock + renewal protection

Team — reading the deck and the economics. I am prepared to provide conditional executive approval with the following firm guardrails. This will require a short memo to CFO for countersignature (I can prepare).

Firm approval terms (do not change without re-escalation):
1) Commercial concessions: up to 25% blended discount in year 1, up to 12% in year 2, year 3 at no more than 7% additional off list. This is a three-year committed contract with revenue recognition consistent with upfront payment schedule.
2) Price lock: guaranteed for 24 months on all subscribed SKUs listed in SOW_v3. Any new SKUs released during the locked period are excluded unless explicitly added to SOW by amendment.
3) Renewal protection: upon renewal, total list-price uplift cannot exceed 7% for the first renewal term; thereafter Redwood may apply standard market pricing. Legal to include CPI-based floor/ceiling language to handle macro swings.
4) Capacity overages: if usage exceeds committed capacity by >20% in a rolling 90-day window, Redwood reserves right to charge overage rates or require upgrade to next tier pricing (not retroactive).
5) Mutual termination: customer may terminate for material breach with 60 days notice; Redwood retains right to deny termination if material payment obligations remain.

Next actions: Tessa — prepare Exec_Approval_Memo summarizing the above, include the Deal Econ, SOW_redlines_3yr.docx, and a proposed DocuSign envelope with the prepayment schedule. Ben — add a line to the SOW clarifying SKU list. Legal will circulate final redlines. I will route to CFO for sign-off once the memo is assembled.

Laura Bennett
SVP, Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Exec_Approval_Memo.pdf (pdf, 1 page)]
